prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
Done. The print's page tab is closed (only a stale about:blank entry remains in the tab list; the CDP target is already gone).

**[goal]** Single-file 3D wallpaper copying Hokusai's woodblock print, plus a record of what was taken from it.

**[action]**
- Inspected `./print.jpg` visually: a giant claw-crested wave at left, three long rowboats (one in the trough under the wave, one cresting the right swell, one on the foreground swell), small snow-capped Mount Fuji at center, Prussian-blue / cream-paper / grey-sky palette.
- Built `./scene/index.html`: one file, Three.js 0.170.0 from the allowed jsdelivr CDN, Google Fonts caption only. Everything is geometry and vertex colors, no texture: animated sine sea grid with quantized woodblock color bands, a curling great-wave ribbon with foam claws (instanced cones) and spray, three low-poly boats with rowers that bob and pitch on the sampled sea height, snow-capped Fuji cone, paper/grey gradient sky, drifting clouds. Gentle motion: sea swell, wave breathing, boat bobbing, spray and cloud drift, slow camera sway.
- Wrote `./result.json`: `boats: 3`, `mountain: "Mount Fuji"`, plus palette and motion notes.
- Verified live: opened the file in the browser three times, screenshotted each revision (framing, wave read, foam balance), final render confirmed with a live canvas and running animation loop (`{"ok":true, frames>0}`, no console crash across renders).

**[result]** `./scene/index.html` renders the recognizable composition (great wave left, Fuji center, three boats) in the print's palette with gentle motion; `./result.json` records boats=3 and mountain=Mount Fuji.

**[next]** None required. Open limits: the wave reads as a stylized slab-and-claw rather than the print's fine fractal foam (low-poly budget), and the three revision rounds were spent on framing and wave readability; further polish (denser claw rows, asymmetric foam streaks) is optional.
